Data checks for a provider model

Source: R/data_checks.R
pp_check.Rd

Missing values, (near-)zero variance of covariates, pairwise correlation among covariates and variance inflation factors. pp_data() runs these checks when check = TRUE; the function is exported for exploratory use.

Usage

pp_check(
  data,
  y,
  x,
  provider,
  n = NULL,
  cor_threshold = 0.9,
  vif_threshold = 10,
  message = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

a data frame.

y

name of the outcome column: 0/1 for a binary outcome, the number of events out of n trials for a binomial outcome, or any numeric value for a continuous outcome. NULL for a survival outcome, which is given by time and event.

x

names of the covariate columns. Covariates must be numeric; code factors as 0/1 columns first.

provider

name of the provider identifier column.

n

name of the column with the number of trials per row (binomial outcome), or NULL.

cor_threshold

warn about pairs of covariates whose absolute correlation exceeds this value. Default 0.9.

vif_threshold

warn about covariates whose variance inflation factor is at least this value. Default 10.

message

print a short summary. Default TRUE.

Value

Invisibly, a list: missing (missing values per column), nzv (near-zero-variance metrics per covariate), cor (correlation matrix), high_cor (pairs above the threshold) and vif.

Details

Missing values in any named column and covariates with zero variance are errors. Near-zero variance (frequency ratio of the two most common values above 95/5 and at most 10% distinct values), high correlation and large VIF are warnings. The VIF of a covariate is \(1/(1 - R^2)\) from regressing it on the other covariates.

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 10, seed = 2)
chk <- pp_check(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider", message = FALSE)
chk$vif
#>       x1       x2       x3 
#> 1.009384 1.002768 1.006736
